utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Ms. D'Ascoli, the next witness is ready?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, he is ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And it's Witness K81. While the witness is brought I could add that his evidence relates to paragraphs 72(i) and 77 of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Are you able to hear the translation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that's given to you now. If you would read that aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will say the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Ms. D'Ascoli has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I would begin --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I would begin by showing you a document which contains some personal information related to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Could the usher please hand this piece of paper to the witness. It is a 65 ter number 02485, and it is the pseudonym sheet for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, please do not read the document aloud. Could you just check whether the information contained in it, is it correct and whether it is an exact description of your identity, your full name, and date and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: It's all correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender this document under seal please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00790, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Witness, I will refer to you with the pseudonym of K81. Mr. K81, did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY in May 1999 and subsequently an addendum to the statement in February 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And before coming to court today, have you had the opportunity to review these statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Did you also testify before this Tribunal in the Milutinovic case in November 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Do you remember that you further corrected your statement during this testimony in the Milutinovic et al. case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And besides the correction -- those corrections that were already made and recorded during the testimony, I understand that during your most recent review of the documents in the proofing session you indicated that there was a spelling mistake still to be corrected in your statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to have on the screen the 65 ter number 02268. And if the Albanian version can be displayed on the screen of the witness, please. Maybe while this is being done, Your Honours, if we could briefly go into private session because I have to correct one of the names of relatives of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. K81, having reviewed this statement and with the correction made to them, are you now satisfied that the information contained in them is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender the witness statement into evidence, please. The unredacted version to be tendered under seal is the 65 ter number 02268.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00791, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And we have also prepared a public redacted version which is the 65 ter number 02526, and I would like to tender that as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned P00792, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. K81, did you also testify before this Tribunal in the Milutinovic et al. case in November 2006; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And before coming to court today, did you have the opportunity to review this -- your previous testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And having reviewed it, if you were asked the same questions would you provide the same answers and testify in the same way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender into evidence also the transcript in the Milutinovic et al. case. And it is the 65 ter number 05069.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned P00793, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I -- yes, please. I see my learned colleague on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one explanation regarding the correction of the name that was made a minute ago. In the statement itself, we have the last name of this person and also the names of many of this person's relatives, and we were in a private session. Now tell me, when I want to mention these names do I have to ask for a private session, or can I use the statement that has not been redacted? Because I think that two paragraphs of the statement are linked together, therefore I am a little bit perplexed with our going into private session and the mentioning of the names that appear in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli, what do you propose?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I would propose that any time my learned colleague seeks to refer to names of either the witness or the witness family or any feature which could be -- which could identify his identity, I would prefer that we go into private session just to avoid any possible identification of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That would seem to be the logical position. I'm afraid if you're dealing with names, we'll need to be in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it seems that you didn't understand me. This person is not a close relative to the witness. This person has a completely different last name and other relatives appear too. I'm not referring to the family of the witness. It goes without saying that this is not going to be mentioned because his identity has not been revealed in public, but this is a completely different surname and completely different group of people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We certainly did misunderstand you, Mr. Djurdjic. We understood you were speaking about family members of the witness. If there is a name which is not a name of the witness and if the statement doesn't describe that person as a relative of the witness, then you may use the name in public session.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if I can specify that in my understanding the names that we've been dealing with in the statement are cousins of the witness. That's why I asked to go into private session even if they have a different last name --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your understanding may be one thing, it's whether the statement or evidence identifies that family relationship. If it is the case, well then we need to be in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I think the statement does, Your Honours, in the previous paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm afraid private session, Mr. Djurdjic, because in the statement it's mentioned that the person, even though with a different name, is a cousin. Previous paragraph I am told. I don't know the name of the person yet, so there's no point in me looking. Move on, please, Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes. Thanks, Your Honours. I would also seek to tender an exhibit associated with Mr. K81's testimony in the Milutinovic et al. case, and it is the 65 ter number 05070. And I can indicate that it is a map of the Gnjilane municipality marked by the witness during his testimony. And I would seek to tender it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00794, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. I can now provide a summary of this witness's evidence. The witness is from the village of Vladovo in the Gnjilane municipality. He describes the entry of the VJ and armed civilians into his village area on the 25th of March, 1999, and their activities which included provocations, setting up check-points, and stealing vehicles. That caused much alarm and, as a result, the witness left his village at the end of March 1999 and went to the village of Vlastica. He stayed in the surrounding mountains with a number of others for two weeks. And from his position he could observe with a pair of binoculars VJ soldiers looting and setting houses on fire in the surrounding area. He also saw the village of Vlastica being attacked, looted, and buildings, including the mosque, being burned by VJ soldiers. After two weeks in the mountains they ran out of food. The witness went to Presevo in Serbia proper and then to the village of Zub. As the VJ was present in that village, people were fleeing towards the village of Sefer. The witness joined these people and they proceeded towards Presevo, then continuing to walk for about 12 hours. The following morning the witness and his group joined many other people who were proceeding towards Macedonia. The police and the VJ escorted the convoy to the border. At the border the police who was escorting the convoy searched the people and took all their ID, papers, and passports. The witness crossed the border into Macedonia in mid-April 1999. This is the end of the in-court summary.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. K81, I now have some questions for you to clarify some parts of your evidence. Sir, in your statement -- and this is for the record. Page 6, paragraph 4, of the English version in e-court and page 2, paragraph 4 of the B/C/S. There you explain that the VJ and some armed civilians came to the area around the village on the 25th of March, 1999, and that you left your village some days later at the end of March. In the last two paragraphs of page 6 and then the first paragraph of page 3, I think, of the B/C/S you -- yeah, you say that when you left the village at the end of March, you went with your family to the village of Vlastica. This is now page 7 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S. First of all, how far is Vlastica from Vladovo and from Zegra?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Llastice is close, about 2 to 3 kilometres further away. From there to the mountain where we went to, it was about 3 to 4 kilometres as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, because in -- at the same page of your statement you describe that you went hiding in the mountains in an area that you called Black Mountain or Kodra e Zeze, which is about 3 or 4 kilometres from your village. So it's my understanding that this mountain area, how far is it from the village of Vlastica, you said like about 2 or 3 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Two to three kilometres is from my village of Vlladove. Llastice is an area from where you could observe very well what's been going on in the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: So is this area that you called the black mountain the area just around the village of Vlastica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. And at page 7 of your statement you describe that during the time that you spent in the mountains you could observe with a pair of binoculars what was happening in the surrounding villages. And you say that you saw soldiers looting, stealing, and setting houses on fire. Can you clarify in which villages this happened? Where did you see the soldiers doing that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: These actions I saw, and that was happening in Llastice, in the village of Llastice, Zheger, and Vlladove.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: So I understand you could clearly observe these three villages, Vladovo, Zegra, and Vlastica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can you tell us what did you see exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I saw the VJ, the police, and some Serb civilians, local Serbs. I saw when they entered the village, they looted the village, they set houses on fire, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And can you describe the way in which you were making these observations from the mountains?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I had binoculars with me. They were members of the Serb army, some policemen, and also local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I think we had a problem in translation because I didn't receive the translation for a substantial part of the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I got to a very convenient place -- to a very convenient place in the mountain where I could see very clearly what was happening in the village, and I could see the people firing. I could see them looting and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And can you clarify which forces were doing what? Because you mentioned three different --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: It was the forces of the VJ. They were wearing regular uniforms. They were also police officers, but also Serb civilians. They were mostly local Serbs. They accompanied the VJ forces and the Serb police.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And how could you distinguish between these different forces, between the police, the VJ, and the civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: From their uniforms. I know very well the uniforms of the army, of the police, and I knew the civilians. They were people who I saw every day before then.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Were the civilians people from your village or from the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: No. They were from Zheger, and one who I managed to identify was from the village of Pasjan.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And at line 19 in replying to one of my questions you said: "Yes, it was the forces of the VJ ..." What do you mean by that? It was the forces of the VJ doing what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Well, the forces of the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. But it was them doing what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: They entered the village. Whoever they got hold of in the village, from that particular village, they man-handled them, they maltreated them, they beat them. And when they were moved out of their -- forced out of their houses, they set the houses on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And did you see this with your eyes, through the binoculars from your positions in the mountains?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes, most of these things I've seen myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And did you see with the VJ these other forces that you mentioned, like the police and the Serbians and the civilians; right? Were they together or --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I see my learned colleague on his feet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously, my learned friend Mrs. D'Ascoli is unhappy with the answers because she's returning the witness to the same question for the third or the fourth time now.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was simply trying to clarify. The witness clarified what the VJ forces were doing, and I was trying to understand what the police and the Serbian civilians were doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. It is a fairly important issue, though, Ms. D'Ascoli and it would be better if you allowed the witness to --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- explain in his words. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. K81, can you clarify -- you mentioned that you saw together with the VJ forces also police and local Serbs. Can you clarify what the police were doing and what the local Serbs were doing, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes. When they would enter the villages in that area, it was first the VJ that would enter the villages. They were together with the local Serbs. They always accompanied the VJ forces. From what I could see, I think that it was the local Serbs that led them first to the houses of the LDK activists at that time. The local Serbs would point out the houses of the most prominent LDK local activists.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. That's clearer now. What about the police forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: They would stay together, but as I said the VJ forces would go first and then they would follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have to react. You instructed my learned friend how to put her questions, and she asked a question, and when the witness answered the way he did, she's coming back to the same question for the fourth time now. I don't mind the witness will probably say the same thing again, but I think this is really not appropriate to insist so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber is not concerned with the questioning, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And if that can help, I was going on with the questions because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No need to go on, Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We could always change our mind if you talk to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. So you said that the police forces would stay together with the VJ; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And did -- what did you see they were doing? Were they just there in the village -- I mean, if you can be a little bit more specific, if you can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: They would enter the village, fire their automatic rifles, they would enter into Albanian houses. Wherever they could find residents, they would beat them, loot them, then they would force them out, then they would loot the houses, and finally they would set them on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: But which forces are you talking about now? Because I think you mentioned "these" --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: The Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm sorry to insist, but did you see the police doing anything or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: No. When the army stationed there, the police would stay there with them. They were all staying together in the villages, the VJ, the police forces, and the local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. K81, in the last paragraph of page 7 of your statement and page 3 -- sorry, paragraph 3 of page 4 of the B/C/S, when you're speaking of the attack that you see on the village of Vlastica, you also mentioned that they burned the mosque. Is it something that you see yourself? And what do you mean by "they"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes. When the army came to the village, first they set the mosque on fire and then the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And this is something, again, you observed through the binoculars from the mountains?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes, I saw this myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to show you a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: It's the 65 ter number 01785. If we can have it on the screen, please. And if we can go to page 2 of this exhibit, please. Could you please enlarge the picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. K81, do you recognise the mosque in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes, this is the mosque of Lashtice village.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And how do you recognise it? How are you able to recognise it as the mosque of Llastice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: From the roof. I know exactly from the roof that this is the village of Lashtice village --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction. The mosque of Lashtice village.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: What do you mean by "from the roof"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Most of the mosques have a dome, whereas the mosque in Lashtice village has this kind of roof. You can see it on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That one photo on page 2, Your Honours, will be assigned P00795.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, let's move to the movement -- to the moment when you joined the convoy of people that -- from the village of Presevo were moving towards the Macedonian border, and for the record this is paragraphs 3, 4 at page 9 of the statement, the English version, and the last paragraph page 5 of the B/C/S. Sir, can you describe the convoy and who were the people in this convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: The convoy that we joined in order to go to Macedonia consisted of ethnic Albanians who were leaving Kosova. They were of different ages, they were elderly, women, children in the convoy. When we learned that they were heading towards Macedonia we decided to join that convoy and also to go to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Was the convoy escorted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes, by the Serb police forces and the VJ forces. They escorted the convoy up to Miratovc village. Then they searched us, seized all our personal documents, and left us in the no-man's area on the border with Macedonia. The border was closed at that time, and therefore we remained there until 4.00 a.m. Once the border was opened, we crossed into Macedonia, and sometime early in the morning we arrived at Stankovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Just some questions to clarify what you just said. What do you mean when you say "they" searched us? Which forces are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Those who searched us and seized all our personal documents were the police and army.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Both together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: The army would stay aside because they were always nearby, whereas it was the policemen who searched us and seized our documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And going back to the convoy, how did you learn that these people were going towards Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: When we arrived at Presheve we were thinking of this town as the safest place to stay, but we found out that maltreatment was ongoing there as well, and that's why we decided to leave that place, and we joined the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. And -- while you were in the convoy, were you free to move into any other direction than the one in which the convoy was leaving, was going?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: No. The direction was known already. It was the police and the army that escorted us up to the border. We were under their escort.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And going back to your previous answers, you said that when you arrived in Presheve you found out there that maltreatments were going on. Which maltreatments do you mean, can you clarify that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: When I arrived there I heard that they had maltreated some Albanians that had arrived there from Kosovo. These people had been beaten, their money was taken away, and their tractors and vehicles confiscated.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And by whom, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: By the Serb police and the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, my last questions. When did you return to Kosovo, to your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I returned to Kosova ten months later. From Stankovec I went to Switzerland, and ten months later I returned to my village.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And then what did you see, what did you find when you returned to your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: When I returned in the village, to tell you the truth I was very upset. I saw horrible things that had happened. I learned upon my return that 55 people from the villages nearby were killed. Twenty-five were killed in Llastice village; in Zheger, 13 people killed; seven in Shurdhan village; seven in my village; and three in the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the name of the last village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... All the houses in the nearby villages had been looted, and most of them had been burned down. And this was all carried out by the VJ, by the police forces, and by the local Serb civilians. (redacted) (redacted) He was killed, and his body was never found.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, just for the record, interpreter didn't -- I see my learned colleague on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the last surname erased from the record. We are starting to use names that we had said earlier should not be mentioned. The witness, himself, mentioned the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not able to be sure whether the name mentioned is a relative of the witness or has the same name as the witness. The transcript at the moment doesn't include that name. Are you able to help me, Mr. Djurdjic or Ms. D'Ascoli?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I also wanted to clarify for the record the names of the villages because they have not been recorded, so I can go through those things.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. K81, you mentioned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has been interpreted to me. I heard it, and I see here in line - which line is it? I can't see

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: (redacted), and you said, Your Honours, that as relatives they should not be mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Please, Mr. K81, answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I can explain everything. These are things that I saw with my own eyes, things that happened in my area. And most of these people were people who I knew. Some of them were my relatives --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Just a second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. What we're trying to ensure is that the record doesn't contain any name of a member of your family so that you are not identified. That's what we're discussing at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic has mentioned a particular name. I think line 19 -- page 19, line 3, is where that name should be inserted. Now, is that a name which identifies the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. K81, is the name that you mentioned before when you said that he was killed and his body was never found, is that person a relative of yours or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes, he is a relative of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Well, both at 19, 3, and 19, 22, the name should be redacted. And if it's anywhere else, the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, you're going to clarify the names of some other villages, are you, Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm just trying to go back to the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. K81, you were telling us about what you heard when -- and what you found out when you returned to your village, and you said 55 people from the villages nearby were killed. I'm reading the transcript at page 18, lines 19 until 22. Twenty-five persons were killed in the village of Llastice, and the name is recorded. Thirty-three people in the village of Zegra, is that correct, and seven in which village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Thirteen Zheger; seven in my village, Vlladove; and seven others in Shurdhan village, a village a little bit further up from Zheger. Whereas in the village of Stolice, three other people were killed. I learned about these people that had been killed after I returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Perfect. That's clear now. Thank you. And can I ask you how did you learn about this, or who told you about these killings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: When I returned, people I had stayed with and who I knew very well told me that these people had been killed; there were many people that had been wounded. I was unable to mention that at that time because I know -- I didn't know all their names, but now I know their names. And when I returned I learned about these killings, about the houses that had been looted and burnt, and I visited the families of those who were killed and massacred.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. And in which condition did you find your house when you returned to Vladovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: My house was completely burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. K81, for having answered my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't have further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. D'Ascoli. Mr. Djurdjic, cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. Do you mind if I address you just as Witness without the number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: As you wish. It's okay with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm Veljko Djurdjic, member of the Defence team for the accused, Vlastimir Djordjevic; assisted by Ms. Marie O'Leary, also member of our team. As we speak different languages, I would kindly ask you to wait a little for the typing to finish on the screen when I ask my question before you start answering, so that the interpreters and the court reporter can follow. I'd like to ask you, Witness, bearing in mind that you have given several statements and this is your second time testifying, when was your recollection of the events concerned the best?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: My memory was at its best then, and it is at its best now. I remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How then do you explain - and I'm starting from the end of your testimony - today for the first time you gave us the exact number of persons by villages who were killed, and you told us that you went to see all these families to express your condolences. Why didn't you state that -- okay, in 1999 you couldn't, but in 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, in order to be able to narrate everything that occurred during the war, it will take us at least a week here in this courtroom. So whenever I was asked in more details, What did you see? I did explain and elaborate. But when my statements were taken, I was asked to explain things briefly, and therefore I gave brief answers then. And there are other testimonies, photographs, recordings, corroborating my testimony. There were people from the Red Cross, from the Tribunal. The Prosecutor, Louise Arbour, at the time was there herself on the site of the people that were killed in Lashtice village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. One more thing you mentioned for the first time today was that Albanians were mistreated in Presevo. This is not to be found in your statements. How come? It's not a small matter that people were mistreated in Presevo. Why didn't you mention it before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: As I said, if we were to discuss everything that happened it will take us at least a week here. There was maltreatment, there was intimidation on the part of the Serb police and army. Had there not been any maltreatment problems and other sorts of crimes, I would have remained in Prishtina --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction: In Preshevo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I had my sister there, her in-laws, but there was maltreatment there, and that's why we decided to leave. It's then that I realised that the police wanted to carry out an ethnic cleansing of the whole area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you told us that today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes. I tried to mention it earlier in brief when the police and the army escorted the convoy, they escorted us to -- up to Miratovc, they seized all our documents, and you probably know what all this means. Once they took our documents, their intention was for us never to return to Kosova again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And that's your inference. Let me ask you, did you ever lose your ID card?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: No, I never lost my ID card. They searched the whole population that was there. The police, the Serb police, dressed in uniforms, searched us, and they seized our documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you when you lose an ID card or any other ID paper, are you able normally to have -- to get a duplicate of that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes, of course you can, but at that time they seized, confiscated, our documents. I didn't lose my ID card; they seized it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I asked these questions because of the inference you've made. Am I right in saying, or did I understand you correctly, that you decided to leave Presevo of your own accord?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I said very clearly, I don't know how you interpreted my answer, when I saw that people were leaving the area, the town, we decided to leave too. We left all our property behind to run for our lives, because the police and the army, whoever they came across they would kill them regardless of whether they were children, elderly, or women. This is what they did in Lashtice village, and this is what they did in many other parts of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What means of transport did you use to go from Presevo to Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: We set out on foot, but there were tractors there driven by Serb police up to Presheve. These were tractors that they had previously confiscated from the Albanian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm asking you about the time when you left Presevo to go to Macedonia. Did you use a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: This is what I'm telling you. We set out on foot from Presheve, got to the road, and then they made us board these tractors that they had previously confiscated. They drove us up to Miratovc village, there they searched us, confiscated our documents, and left us there by the border. And from there we proceeded to the border, and from the border on buses and some on foot were taken to Stankovec refugee camp, where we stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me please who accompanied you when you set off from Presevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: The Serb police and the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you travel to Macedonia on your own without your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: No. Together with my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me which members of your family joined you on your trip to Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: It was my close family, also a thousand other people of different ages, other families. In my family it was my wife, my children, my brother, my sisters, and so on. And there were also some cousins of mine who were with us. But the -- the column was long, the column of people was long. It was about a thousand people, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we now move to private session because I intend to ask the witness about some names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you the truth, I don't know how this works. We have adopted a package according to 92 bis containing the statements and addenda. And my infallible associate can help me with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And I'm looking at your statement given on the 1st of February, 2001, but I don't see the venue or the location where you gave this statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, it was in my own home. That was when I had another look at the earlier statement. It was the same statement that I had given in 1999, but we had another look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have cut short the number of my questions. Please can you look at page 2, both in English and Albanian. Mr. Witness, could you please read the lasting paragraph of this statement in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the last page of the statement, both in English and in Albanian. It seems to me that a moment ago we had an English version and not an Albanian one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If I may help you, that is an addendum to your statement given on the 1st of February, 2002, which is in the package with the first statement. But Ms. O'Leary has told me that this is page 1. There are some odd numbers attached to these documents in the 92 bis package. Actually, I have it written down somewhere. The Albanian version was entered from pages 5 to 13, so this could be either the 13th or the fifth page, or rather, the end of the statement. I'm talking about the 1st of February, 2002, statement, and it begins with witness statement and has only one page.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I can assist. I think if my colleague is looking for the statement of 2002 in the Albanian version, this is -- this starts at page 14 of the Albanian version in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Please, the end of the statement in Albanian is on page 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you now read the last paragraph of this document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Can you enlarge the statement a bit because I cannot make out what it reads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you want it read aloud, Mr. Djurdjic? Can you read that aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "I have more information about what happened to me, my family, and my village, that is, more information that I've stated in this statement."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I obviously received a wrong translation. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, without mentioning any names, can you tell us who you were living with in the same household in March 1999? You can only give us the type of the relation that you had with these people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: With my wife, three children, my brother, my father and mother, and my three sisters. One brother was in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was your father in Switzerland or in Vladovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that you mentioned that he had been in Vladovo. Your paternal grandfather, do you remember him? Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes. He wasn't there because he died in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In March 1999 what did you do for living?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I worked at a grocer's shop, and that's where I lived. During -- during the war that was looted and burned down. And I was also supported by my father who was working abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I was interested in the period before the war. Tell me, did you own that shop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: That was before, before the war, I was working into my own grocer's shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me this: The house where you used to live, did it have a yard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was the yard fenced or surrounded by a wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes, a small wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me the height of the wall and what it was made of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: It was about 1.4, 1.5 metres high.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What was it made of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: It was just a normal wall. It wasn't a very special kind of wall. Concrete blocks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there a gate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How high was the gate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: 2.5 metres, that was the height.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I see from your statement that you continued your education after the secondary school. Which school did you attend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: It was a communications school to become a driving instructor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's actually a course for driving instructors; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Since several questions were put to you to which you replied by saying police/army, police/army, your statement that you gave in May in 1999 you mentioned police for the first time on page 3 of that statement. And if I'm not mistaken you have made reference to Stanko and Buda Milkovic, and you said that these were the two policemen that you saw in uniforms, dark blue uniforms, and you mentioned them again towards the end when you arrived at the border.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I didn't see them when I went to the border, but I saw them when they were wandering around the villages in Llastice, in Zheger, and Vlladove.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I apologise, I was not precise enough. I wanted to say that in your 1999 statement, you mentioned police twice. That is when I mentioned Milkovic and this other person, and the second time you mentioned them when you were crossing the border. However, today I heard you saying that in addition to army, you saw police forces as well, and you said that on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But that was not the case when you gave your statement in 1999 and when you made corrections in 2002. You didn't correct your statement in that sense?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: When the Serbian army started the offensive, they were accompanied by the Serb police and the local Serbs. I said it then and I'm saying it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I told you specifically where you mentioned them the first time and the second time; however, during your evidence today you mentioned them more than twice. You made corrections in 2000 and now, today, you're telling us that you saw police along the army in every place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I've seen them all the time, and they were together all the time, but I haven't had a chance to give those details. The police station was in Zheger, and the police forces were always there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about your statement, page 9, paragraph 2; and in English, page 8, paragraph 1, which is when Milkovic and this other person are mentioned first. And the second mention was - but you already explained that - the second mention appears in the penultimate paragraph. Given that you have provided us with an explanation, we can move on. Am I right to say that in addition to the forces that you described, you saw people in civilian clothes as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes. They had -- some of them had either the jacket or the trousers from the army, but I recognised these people whose uniform, half of it was civilian, half of it was military, I recognised them because I knew them. I knew they were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that you never served in the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what military reservists are and military reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I don't know the details, but I've been told that the reserve forces are called to join the regular forces whenever they're needed. The reserve force is there to help in case of need. I'm not very accurate in what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I didn't expect anything more. Tell me, were you politically active before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you know what the DSK was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes. LDK was an Albanian party which operated at the time. Even if you asked a little child about the LDK, they'd be able to explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you were not a member of the LDK; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: All Albanians were members of the LDK -- Albanian party.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1999 and before, were you acquainted with Mr. Qamil Shabani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: By name, yes, but not in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you met him in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you just tell us briefly how did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I knew that he was from Zheger, but I hadn't talked to him. I hadn't met him in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think this is a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have the first break now and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, my last question before the break to which I didn't get an answer was this: After the war did you meet Mr. Shabani Qamil; and if you did, under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: As I said earlier, I knew him by sight, but I never met him earlier and I never talked to him, engaged in any conversation with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean to this day you have not met him? To this day you only know him by sight and you never talked to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I did meet him and speak with him, but not immediately after the war. This is how I understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I said after the war did you meet him; and if so, under what circumstances? And since you say now that you did meet him --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Not immediately after the war, as I said, but later on I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When, where, and under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I met him in Zheger. Monday is a market day in Zheger, and that's where I saw him and greeted him, but I don't know the exact circumstances and the exact dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you seen him perhaps here, in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Two days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: At this time in Zegra when you met him, when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Much later. I don't remember the dates but I recognised him. He was older and I greeted him, to show him respect. My village and Zheger village are close by, and that's where I completed my school, and I used to travel on that road very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you met him and you talked, did you touch upon the subject of his status as a witness before this Court? Did you mention to each other that you have given statements and he has given statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I spoke with him. I told him, Good for you, that you went there and told the truth and what happened in our villages. There was no need for me to discuss in detail his statement. He had his own statement, own testimony; I had my statement, my testimony. There was no need for me to discuss his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he tell you perhaps when he first gave a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't ask him about his testimony, but I did see him giving one on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I asked you this because in certain details your evidence is complementary, but we'll talk about that later. I'd now like to move to your statement of 1999 to clear up certain points. That's Exhibit P791. Witness, in paragraph 2 you say when you were giving that statement: "I have been in the refugee camp since 15 April 1999 ..." When did you return to Kosovo from that camp and where exactly did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: From the refugee camp I went to Switzerland, and some ten months afterwards I returned to Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You go on to say in paragraph 7, that should be page 7 in Albanian and page 6 in English, you say that you heard one man was shot at in Zegra. Did I understand correctly you were not an eye-witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I heard, that this person was shot, that they had gone to his house, that the police took him to the police station. He went to the police station to tell what had happened. The police just fooled around, mocked him, and then they went back to the village, took also his wife, and they -- he was shot. The police and the army also went to the houses of other LDK activists such as Tahir, but Tahir happened not to be in his house. They killed his brother Shyqeri there and wounded his sister. Then they went to look for Nehat, who was also an LDK activists, but he happened not to be in the house. They killed his brother, his aunt, and stole 1.000 Deutschemarks from that house. It was the police, army, and the VJ that did this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And who told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I heard from the villagers. I was in Vlladove village, but I would go to Zheger village occasionally whenever I could move. This was the reason -- accidents like that were the reasons for the people to start leaving because whoever was found in the villages by the police, they were killed, and this is why I left, and this is why others left in the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My question was: Who told you that? And another question would be: Who told you the surname of that person, of that man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I didn't know his last name, but I heard the name from those people who were familiar with this incident. They said that the name was Ukshin, but I didn't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We heard all the same things from the witness Shabani; that's why I'm asking you this. Tell me, do you know what KLA is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: The KLA was an army that was formed by the people themselves and it was formed, established, to defend the population. In our area there was no KLA. There were only unprotected civilians in my area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How do you know there was no KLA presence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: This I know because I was in these villages all the time. My family was there. I moved about in the area, went to the hills, to the mountains, and I didn't see any people who I saw in this area were all civilians, villagers, family people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that, in your book, if a person is wearing civilian clothes he is not a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: That's correct, because they were all unarmed. They didn't have uniforms, they didn't have weapons. They were civilians, people with their families staying in their own homes. They were forced to leave their houses for security reasons and take to the mountains for their -- to protect their own lives, leaving behind all their valuables and property. The reason for this was that the Serb police and the army, whoever they would find in their own homes they would kill them and do the worst things to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, we have all your statements, both those given to the investigators and the evidence given before the Court; therefore, let's not waste time and repeat things. My next question is: How do you know the dress code of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I don't know that because I didn't see them in my village and the surrounding villages. Personally, I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, then you can only infer because based on all your answers so far you don't seem to know whether there were any KLA in your village or not.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: There wasn't any because there were no people armed in the area. Those who were armed were only the policemen, the army, and the local Serbs. Not a single Albanian had a uniform or a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Not a single Albanian had a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Not a single one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, did the DSK exist in your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes. As in other places in the world, you have a party with its branches in municipalities, in smaller areas, so we did have a branch. And the LDK activists were the first ones to be targeted by the forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you attend the funeral of this man, Ukshin, we discussed a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you go to any meetings in this period between the 23rd and the 30th, some meetings of the DSK in your village where the attendees consulted and made certain conclusions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: No. There weren't such meetings convened at any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would I be right in saying you have no first-hand knowledge of the events in Zegra village regarding the members of the DSK; you only heard about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: As I said earlier, I heard for most of this incident, but I did see many things while I was observing the area through my binoculars. I saw the VJ presence, the police, and the local Serbs and what they did. I could see through the binoculars the police and the army that entered the village and emptied it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now ask for the 65 ter exhibit 0036. Can we zoom in on the lower part from Gnjilane downwards. A bit higher up. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, would you draw a line below your village.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Can you enlarge it a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is asking if this can be zoomed in further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot read it very well. Can you please zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and please scroll it down a bit so we can see Gnjilane. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Draw a thin line below the place where you lived.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: This is Vlladove.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Put a number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now draw another line, please, below Zegra.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, below Zegra, where you see the words Zegra.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Put number 2 there, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now please draw a line below Vlastica and number 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, could you please draw a line where this black mountain was, if that's what it's called.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now at the beginning of this line put XX.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: The line that I've drawn here is the mountainous area where I've stayed, it's here, that's Kodra e Zeze.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I understand, but so that we know that it's this precisely, put an X at the end of that line. You drew a semicircle. Put an X at the beginning of the line, and an X at the end of the line, and number 4 at the other end as well, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And next to it number 4 so we know from the record that it's the mark for the black mountain.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, where is Pecane village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I cannot see the name here, but it's further up towards Presheve, but the name hasn't been marked here because it's only the Presheve area. Can you please move it further up, the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid we will lose it then -- no, this can't be done. So Pecane is north of Gnjilane; is that what you're saying? You see Gnjilane is this yellow circle. We see part of it at the top.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... top of here. It should be around here. Pecan should be around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This X you placed, is that Pecane? Oh, so then it's not north of Gnjilane?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: It should be roughly here, it should be roughly here because the name hasn't been marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then put number 5 there, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about Sefer village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Somewhere near here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Put number 6 there, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In your statement there is a reference to Zub village. Where is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Roughly here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Put number 7, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Can you please move the map further up. Maybe the names are marked there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We cannot move electronically without losing the markings that you have made unfortunately. Do you have more villages you want marked, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more place that we can't see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Show us the direction of Presevo on this map. Just put an arrow.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Presheve should be in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... so we know that that is the direction of Presevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned D00116, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, which members of your family did you drive from Vladovo to Vlastica in March 1999 when you decided ... ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: My sisters, my mother, my brother, my wife, the children.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many of your sisters set off with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And where did you take them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: We went to the mountain to escape the army, to hide there in the mountains, so that we did not suffer the worst, as many others did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you all went to the black mountain, the entire family; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you travel to the black mountain? Did you have any means of transportation, or did you walk up there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: We went by car up to a point closer to the road where we got off, and then we continued on foot, and then later we learned that the car had been taken by the army, and I've never seen that since.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have now to put to you the following, and that's paragraph 11 in my copy; and in the Albanian version it's the page, page 7, last paragraph; and in English, it's page 7 and 3. You said that you took your family to Vlastica and then spent the night --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear where he spent the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us what is the right description or what happened to you and your family.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Can you please ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I read out to you part of your statement in which you say that you took your family to the village of Vlastica and that you, yourself, went to the mountain alone. Today you told us that you took your family directly to the mountain in -- and not to the village.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I took my family, all my family, to the mountains. Once I settled them there, then I returned to the village to see what was happening because we had valuables, we had things, and I spent another night there and then I left. After that night I had no other opportunity to go back to my home, to my house, because the army had moved in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I understand about your house and you, but you didn't leave your family in the Vlastica village but rather on the mountain; there is a difference between these two statements. As far as I understand you did have some relatives in the village of Vlastica, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: No, no, that's not correct. Kodra e Zeze is part of the village of Llastice. That's what I meant. That's what I meant when I mentioned that. It was of Kodra e Zeze of the village of Llastice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but today you told us that there was 2 kilometres between Vlastica and the mountain, or rather, that between Vladovo and Vlastica is up to 3 kilometres, and the distance to the mountain is 3 to 4 kilometres, so we cannot be speaking about one and the same geographical --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: But Kodra e Zeze is part of Llastice. Kodra e Zeze is part of Llastice. That is where my family settled, in the mountainous area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From these mountains, how did you observe Vlastica, Vladovo, and Zep [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: It was a mountainous area and the Zheger is surrounded by the mountains area, and I could get to the closest point there where I could observe clearly what was going on in the village. So I had to move around the mountainous area to find a convenient and clear observation point to see what was happening in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What did you use to observe the village and the buildings in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I had a pair of binoculars, and they helped me to see things more clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what was the make of that binoculars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I don't know what make the binoculars were, but they were very good binoculars.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How many of you used these binoculars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I used the binoculars.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Only you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I used it, but when there was a friend of mine with me, I lent them to -- the binoculars to my friend to have a look, but then I got it back and I used it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, this vantage point from which you were observing, was that the same place where your family was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: When I was observing the village, what was going on in the village, it was -- I was higher up on the mountainside, and I moved to the points which was clearer and nearer the areas which I wanted to observe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please, first listen to my question and then give me an answer. I put you a very simple question. Was that vantage point from which you were observing the same place where your family was? Just answer me with yes or no. This is just for the sake of expediency and for saving time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: My family was close by, and I left the family stationed at one point, and then I moved closer to a point where I could see clearly. My family was settled somewhere on the Kodra e Zeze, and I personally moved to points which helped me observe clearly what was going on in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please move into private session because I intend to make reference to some names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, so with these binoculars you were able to see everything that was going on in your village of Vladovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Most of the things going on there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you describe what you saw with regards to the mosque. What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: The villagers that had remained in the houses, elderly people, were collected and brought there until the operation was completed. Six persons were killed there, Zijadin Mahmuti, Beqir Mahmuti, Daut Mahmuti. At the entry to the village, Ahmet, Ganimete, and Hevzi were killed. And until that evening they carried out looting, burning, and then they ordered these people to bury the bodies and never to return to their homes in the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You were asked about the mosque. Are you saying these events occurred at the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the vicinity of the mosque these elderly people that were found in the village were gathered, were brought there by the forces and were left there until the operation of the forces was completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My question was: What did you see happen to the mosque?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Nothing happened at that particular moment to the mosque, but something happened to the people that were brought there, the elderly people that were brought there were maltreated. I'm talking about the mosque in Vlladove village, whereas in Llastice, when they entered the village the first thing that they set on fire was the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now we've come to Vlastica. So nothing happened to the mosques in Vladovo. And what did you see happen to the mosque in Vlastica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: When the army entered the village, the police and the local Serbs in Llastice, first thing they did was set the mosque on fire, then they looted the houses, set them afire, maltreated the people who they found in their homes, and did everything else that I've already explained. I could see this clearly when these incidents happened, not only this particular incident but every incident that I've described in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, when I ask you about mosques, if you have seen something I would like you to describe it. I don't want you to just tell me as a statement, The mosque was burned down. Tell me what was set on fire, how, what happened as you were looking. That's what I want to hear.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I'm repeating this so many times now, but I will keep repeating as much as you want. When the army entered the house accompanied by the police and the local Serbs, first thing they did was to set alight the mosque in Llastice village. Then they started to loot the houses, to set them alight, to maltreat and kill the people who they found in their homes --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please, stop there. Please. Tell me what you saw. How did you see the mosque set on fire? That's what I want to hear from you. I don't want you to repeat the same thing for the fifth time. Tell me what was set on fire, where, please describe it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: When the army accompanied by the police and the local Serbs entered the village, they set out towards the mosque. They set it on fire. I saw the flames coming out, and when you see a facility set on fire you can see the flames. Everything can see that. Then they continued to the houses, they looted them, they set them alight, they maltreated the people they found in them, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you see fire on the outside of the mosque from your vantage point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: Yes, I could see the flames and the smoke coming out of the windows of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And did you see fire on the outside, flames on the outside, or did you just see smoke?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I saw flames, and I saw smoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me what burned on the mosque?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: The inside of the mosque was burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you saw from the outside that the inside of the mosque was burning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K81
utterances.text: I told you that the smoke and the flames were coming out from the mosque, and this is a fact, that the mosque in Llastice was burnt, and I saw it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We have a document here from which one can see that there were -- there was damage from the smoke inside the mosque but nothing on the outside.
